findings.summary: An installed native connection callback can replace the raw socket inside the retained OwnedSocket before send target resolution. The final check compares that replacement to the currently resolved raw target, while first_sockets records the wrapper only. Native encoding sends the admitted credential through the replacement; the pre-existing foreign variant is also closed by cleanup. Both class and lambda factories reproduce.
findings.repair_scope: Retain original raw socket identity and ownership across the lifetime, validate it at the actual effect, and settle only originally owned handles.
findings.classification_limit: Only synthetic admitted owned key; no foreign secret observed

findings.summary: A get_method callback replaces or removes the originally attached catalog admission before Connection.request freezes expected_carrier. The retained authority remains valid, but the newly captured carrier is then accepted at wire and return. Both native class and lambda paths return models.
findings.repair_scope: Retain original request carrier at entry, before any request callback, and compare identity throughout native dispatch and effects.
findings.classification_limit: Identity contract observation; this control did not expose foreign secret or owner/session substitution.

findings.summary: Cached native refusal, new foreign socket refusal, and factory cancellation clear ownership maps and close owned handles, but the preserved exception traceback retains Connection.__init__.prior_objects. The temporary weak reference remains alive after transport closure in both HTTP and HTTPS. Source frames retain 26,275–28,319 objects in the focused proof. Success releases the snapshot, and closed wrappers reject later sends.
findings.repair_scope: Release snapshot locals on all failed constructor/adoption paths while preserving the original exception and the anti-ID-reuse ownership protection.
findings.classification_limit: FD/response/buffer/socket/thread closure passes. Snapshot graph lifetime fails while the causal exception is retained; finite interpreter exit ends fixture ownership.
